parsed.why: No trans-specific offence and 2020 repeal leave no criminal statute, but no recognition, no anti-discrimination law, military rule, common individual harassment and documented (non-widespread) police 'modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming people; no protective machinery, no trans-violence data.

Enforced sodomy law (14 years) used as police lever: documented pretext detention, on-the-spot extortion, rape by officers, forced anal exams, birth-sex custody practice; pending death-penalty Family Bill. Court gains are resident-facing; recourse recurringly unremedied.

No criminalisation, but acceptance 5/100, no anti-discrimination law, ambiguous hate-crime cover, 2024 report of torture, sexual violence and extortion against LGBT people, arson met with 12-hour police response, legislators calling for a trans woman to be burned alive.

No criminalisation and visible community/court gains, but implementation gaps: provincial trans people face public and institutional discrimination plus frequent physical and sexual harassment, conversion therapy, and escalating political homophobic speech with supporter death threats.

Thin record. Structured positive: no criminalisation, 2018 constitutional equality guarantee, dated stigma only. No documented state targeting, no LGR or complaint machinery documented; conservative island society and unenforced guarantee temper the score.
